## 

Scatter Plot

- Used to observe relationships between two continuous variables.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
data(mtcars)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = 'blue') +
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot: Weight vs MPG",
       x = "Car Weight", y = "Miles per Gallon")
```



## 

Bar Chart (Column Plot)

- Useful for categorical comparisons.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar(fill = 'steelblue') +
  labs(title = "Number of Cars by Cylinder Count",
       x = "Cylinders", y = "Count")
```


## 

Correlation Matrix

- Visualizes relationships among multiple numerical variables.

```{r}
library(ggcorrplot)
corr_matrix <- cor(mtcars)
ggcorrplot(corr_matrix, lab = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Correlation Matrix of mtcars Dataset")
```

## 

Facet Plot

- Allows splitting data into multiple panels based on a categorical variable.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = hp)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cyl) +
  labs(title = "Facet Plot: MPG vs HP by Cylinders")
```

## 

Combined Plot (ggarrange)

- Useful for summarizing multiple graphs in one visualization.

```{r}
library(ggpubr)
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) + geom_bar()
ggarrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2, labels = c("A", "B"))
```


## 

Maps & Their Importance

- Maps are essential for **spatial analysis** and decision-making.

```{r warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
world_map <- map_data("world")
ggplot(world_map, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "lightblue", color = "white") +
  coord_fixed(1.3) +
  labs(title = "World Map")
```
